title: RoofLang: enabling AI-driven architecting of LLM inference systems
org: Ziyue Yang, Yuting Jiang, Lei Qu, Peng Cheng
gist: Argues that agent loops driven by profiling can only tune the stack they are handed. It proposes a small language for describing inference workloads, a set of changes that can be checked, and an evaluator that does not depend on any one implementation, so an agent can search whole architectures. A persistent agent is reported to have found designs that raise throughput and interactivity on a current model.
changes: An attempt at the thing C4 says is missing: a cheap way to judge a design without building and benchmarking it. If it holds up, evaluation stops being the bottleneck for architecture-level search.
caveats: Abstract only. The agent-found gains (6 to 50%) have no named baseline, so they are not in the ledger. Nothing says the evaluator's predictions were checked against a real engine under real traffic.

bears_on.note: Proposes an evaluator independent of any implementation. Unproven, but a direct attempt at the cheap oracle.
By the authors' account, a persistent agent found new architectures for a current model and chip, not only settings.

retired_why: A proposed evaluator that needs no implementation. A simulator checked against real hardware now makes the point with numbers. Its roster entry stays.
